title: FLG Q1 Earnings Beat on NII Growth, Stock Dips as Fee Income Falls Y/Y
content:
Flagstar Bank, National Association FLG reported first-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings per share of 4 cents, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 3 cents. In the year-ago quarter, the company had incurred a loss of 23 cents.

Results were primarily driven by an improvement in net interest income (NII), no provision for credit losses, and lower expenses. However, a decline in non-interest income acted as a headwind. Given the concern, FLG shares lost 2.2% during Friday’s trading session.

Results excluded certain non-recurring items. After considering these, the net income available to common shareholders (GAAP basis) was $13 million against a net loss of $108 million in the prior-year quarter.

FLG’s Quarterly Revenues Rise & Expenses Decline

Quarterly revenues were $498 million, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 10.6%. The metric rose 2% from the prior-year quarter.

NII was $443 million, up 8% year over year. The net interest margin (NIM) of 2.15% expanded 41 basis points from the year-ago quarter, driven by a lower cost of funds and balance sheet repositioning.

Non-interest income was $55 million, which declined 31% from the year-ago quarter. The decrease was mainly due to lower fee income, reduced loan-related income, and the impact of prior mortgage servicing business sales.

Non-interest expenses of $466 million decreased 12% year over year. Adjusted operating expenses were $441 million, down 9% from the first quarter of 2025, reflecting lower compensation, FDIC insurance, and general administrative costs.

Flagstar Financial’s Loans Decrease & Deposits Increase

Total loans and leases held for investment declined nearly 1% sequentially to $60.4 billion as of March 31, 2026. As of the same date, total deposits increased 1% sequentially to $66.8 billion.

FLG’s Credit Quality: Improving Trend

Non-accrual loans were $2.7 billion, which decreased from $3.3 billion as of March 31, 2025. Net charge-offs were $78 million, which declined 32% from the prior-year quarter.

The company recorded nil provisions for credit losses compared with $79 million recorded in the year-ago quarter.

Flagstar Financial’s Capital Ratios Strengthen

As of March 31, 2026, the common equity tier 1 ratio was 13.24% compared with 11.90% as of March 31, 2025. The total risk-based capital ratio increased to 16.69% from 15.25% in the prior-year quarter.

The leverage capital ratio rose to 9.61% from 8.45% a year ago, reflecting improved capital strength.

Our View on FLG

Flagstar Financial’s continued reduction in commercial real estate exposure and improving credit quality remain encouraging. While lower non-interest income and balance sheet contraction persist as concerns, solid C&I loan growth, margin expansion, declining credit costs, and disciplined expense management supported another quarter of profitability. Notably, recent credit rating upgrades by Fitch and Moody’s reflect improving confidence in the bank’s balance sheet strength, profitability outlook, and ongoing business transformation. Continued execution on balance sheet optimization and revenue diversification will be key to sustaining this positive momentum.

title: VLY Q1 Deep Dive: Deposit Growth and Technology Investments Support Outlook
content:
Regional banking company Valley National Bancorp (NASDAQ:VLY) announced better-than-expected revenue in Q1 CY2026, with sales up 12.6% year on year to $540.4 million. Its non-GAAP profit of $0.29 per share was 5.7% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

Is now the time to buy VLY? Find out in our full research report (it’s free).

Valley National Bank (VLY) Q1 CY2026 Highlights:

Revenue: $540.4 million vs analyst estimates of $534.7 million (12.6% year-on-year growth, 1.1% beat) Adjusted EPS: $0.29 vs analyst estimates of $0.27 (5.7% beat) Market Capitalization: $7.63 billion

StockStory’s Take

Valley National Bancorp’s first quarter saw positive market reaction, as the company outpaced Wall Street’s revenue and profit expectations. Management cited robust core deposit growth and disciplined loan expansion across key commercial and healthcare verticals as fundamental drivers. CEO Ira D. Robbins highlighted ongoing investments in technology and data infrastructure, noting that recent enhancements have strengthened Valley National Bancorp’s operating model and competitive positioning, especially in specialty deposit verticals and treasury management services.

Looking ahead, management’s guidance is built on expectations of continued strength in core deposit gathering, disciplined loan growth concentrated in business banking and healthcare, and careful capital allocation. CFO Travis P. Lan stated the bank anticipates net interest income and loan growth to trend toward the upper end of previous ranges, aided by a stable funding profile and repricing tailwinds. The company sees further operational leverage from technology investments, with Robbins emphasizing that “AI capabilities will continue to translate into higher productivity, better risk outcomes, and a more consistent client experience.”

Key Insights from Management’s Remarks

Management attributed the quarter’s performance to strong core deposit inflows, relationship-driven loan origination, and operational improvements stemming from technology investments.

Deposit franchise expansion: Valley National Bancorp emphasized its focus on building a high-quality, resilient funding base, with direct customer deposits growing significantly. This allowed the company to reduce reliance on costlier brokered deposits and Federal Home Loan Bank advances, which management described as essential for supporting growth across market cycles. Loan growth in targeted sectors: The company prioritized lending to business banking, middle market, and healthcare, with a disciplined approach that included exiting lower-return transactional client relationships. Management highlighted that the healthcare vertical, in particular, continues to deliver differentiated value and durable demand. Expense control and efficiency: Despite seasonal payroll tax headwinds, the bank maintained flat adjusted noninterest expenses by cutting other compensation and professional fees. The efficiency ratio improved to 53.1%, reflecting operational discipline and a commitment to further positive operating leverage throughout the year. AI integration into operations: Valley National Bancorp’s early investments in artificial intelligence and data analytics are now embedded in its operating model. AI-driven tools are being used for client outreach, fraud detection, and process optimization in underwriting and risk monitoring, which management expects will drive productivity and enhance customer experience. Capital strategy and buybacks: The bank generated over 30 basis points of regulatory capital in the quarter, using a portion to repurchase shares while maintaining capital ratios at the high end of its target range. Management indicated buybacks may be moderated in the coming quarters to prioritize funding high-quality loan growth as opportunities arise.

Story Continues

Drivers of Future Performance

Valley National Bancorp expects future performance to be driven by core deposit growth, disciplined loan origination, and operating leverage from technology investments, amid a competitive funding environment and evolving interest rate backdrop.

Sustained deposit momentum: Management projects deposit growth to reach the high end of its 5% to 7% annual range, supported by a mix of commercial and small business relationships. The company aims to further reduce funding costs by shifting away from wholesale funding in favor of core deposits, which is expected to stabilize the net interest margin. Loan growth in targeted verticals: The bank anticipates total loan expansion between the midpoint and high end of its 4% to 6% range, with continued emphasis on C&I (commercial and industrial) and healthcare lending. Management views ongoing talent investments and robust pipelines in core markets as drivers of above-market loan demand, while running off lower-return commercial real estate balances. Efficiency and technology gains: Valley National Bancorp expects operating leverage to improve, targeting an efficiency ratio near 50% by year-end. Technology and AI investments are expected to further reduce costs and streamline operations, while potential regulatory changes, such as Basel III, are being monitored for capital impact.

Catalysts in Upcoming Quarters

In the coming quarters, our analysts will closely monitor (1) the pace and sustainability of core deposit growth as the bank continues to rotate away from higher-cost funding, (2) the execution of targeted loan expansion in commercial and healthcare sectors, and (3) ongoing improvements in operating efficiency from technology and AI initiatives. We will also track Valley National Bancorp’s capital management strategy, especially in light of evolving regulatory requirements and any changes in the competitive deposit landscape.

title: VLY Stock Rallies 3.9% as Q1 Earnings Beat on Higher NII & Fee Income
content:
Shares of Valley National Bancorp VLY rallied 3.9% in yesterday’s trading session on better-than-expected quarterly results. Its first-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings per share of 29 cents surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 27 cents. The bottom line also compared favorably with earnings of 18 cents in the year-ago quarter.

Results were primarily aided by increased net interest income (NII) and non-interest income, along with lower provision. Higher loan and deposit balances were other tailwinds. However, elevated expenses remained an undermining factor.

After considering non-recurring items, net income available to common shareholders (GAAP basis) was $156.7 million, which jumped 58.1% from the year-ago quarter.

Valley National’s Revenues Improve, Expenses Rise

Total revenues (fully-taxable-equivalent or FTE basis) were $541.6 million, up 12.9% year over year. The top line beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $532.6 million.

NII (FTE basis) was $472.8 million, up 12.2% year over year. The net interest margin (FTE basis) was 3.17%, which expanded 21 basis points (bps).

Non-interest income jumped 18.1% year over year to $68.8 million. The rise was driven by an increase in almost all fee income components, except for insurance commissions, net gains on securities transactions and other income.

Non-interest expenses of $309.9 million increased 12% year over year. The rise was due to an increase in almost all cost components, except for FDIC insurance assessment costs and costs related to amortization of other intangible assets.

The adjusted efficiency ratio was 53.10%, down from 55.87% in the prior-year quarter. A decline in the efficiency ratio indicates an improvement in profitability.

VLY’s Loans & Deposits Rise

As of March 31, 2026, total loans were $50.8 billion, up 1.4% from the previous quarter. Total deposits were $52.9 billion, up 1.3% sequentially.

Valley National’s Credit Quality: A Mixed Bag

As of March 31, 2026, total non-performing assets were $439.6 million, up 23.4% year over year.

However, allowance for credit losses as a percentage of total loans was 1.18%, down 4 bps year over year. In the first quarter of 2026, VLY reported provision for credit losses of $21.2 million, which decreased 66.1% from the prior-year quarter.

VLY’s Profitability & Capital Ratios Improve

At the end of the first quarter, adjusted annualized return on average assets was 1.05%, up from 0.69% in the year-earlier quarter. Adjusted annualized return on average shareholders’ equity was 8.60%, up from 5.69%.

As of March 31, 2026, the tangible common equity to tangible assets ratio was 8.82%, up from 8.61% in the corresponding period of 2025. Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio was 11.60%, up from 11.53%. Also, the common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 10.91% was up from 10.80% as of March 31, 2025.

Story Continues

Valley National’s Share Repurchase Update

In the reported quarter, VLY repurchased 4 million shares at an average price of $12.95 under its ongoing stock buyback program.

Our Take on VLY

Valley National’s effort to strengthen fee income, higher NII, solid loans and deposit growth, and expansion initiatives are expected to support its financials. However, persistently rising costs and weak asset quality are major concerns.

title: Valley National Bancorp Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
Valley National Bancorp Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Execution and Operational Transformation

Management is deliberately reshaping the organization by strengthening the balance sheet and upgrading the operating model to support long-term value creation. The strategic focus centers on building a resilient funding franchise by winning primary operating relationships rather than pursuing short-term pricing advantages. Capital is being intentionally allocated toward high-demand sectors like healthcare and business banking while selectively exiting lower-return transactional clients. Operational scalability is being driven by past investments in core conversion and data infrastructure, allowing revenue to grow faster than fixed costs. Artificial Intelligence is being integrated to augment associate productivity and enhance decision-making, specifically in underwriting, risk monitoring, and customer service. The bank's approach to AI is underpinned by years of investment in data consistency and granularity, enabling pragmatic use cases like voice AI for collections. Management emphasizes a relationship-led culture where technology preserves the human element while reducing friction in the client experience.

2026 Outlook and Financial Trajectory

Annual net interest income growth is expected to trend toward the higher end of previous guidance, with more meaningful acceleration in the second half of 2026. Loan growth for the year is projected between the midpoint and high end of the 4% to 6% range, supported by a robust C&I pipeline. Total deposit growth is anticipated at the high end of the 5% to 7% range as the bank continues rotating out of higher-cost wholesale funding. The efficiency ratio is targeted to trend toward 50% by 2026, driven by positive operating leverage and disciplined expense control. Management expects the CET1 ratio to remain at the higher end of the 10.5% to 11% target range to support organic growth and potential buybacks.

Structural Dynamics and Risk Factors

The bank utilized approximately one-third of its capital generation for stock buybacks this quarter, though future activity may moderate to support loan growth. Regulatory CRE concentration is trending lower as the bank exits non-relationship transactional loans to improve overall portfolio ROI. A customer-facing voice AI agent was implemented to proactively contact past-due auto loan customers, demonstrating early efficiency gains from automation. Management estimates a potential 80 to 100 basis point increase in regulatory capital ratios under the proposed Basel III standardized approach.

Story Continues

Q&A Session Highlights

NII outlook and funding cost drivers without rate cuts

Management stated they are neutral to the front end of the curve, so the lack of Fed cuts is not overly impactful to their NII outlook. Confidence in margin expansion is driven by the structural rotation of high-cost wholesale funding into lower-cost core deposits.

Capital priorities and future stock buyback activity

The primary priority for capital is supporting high-quality organic loan growth, which may lead to lighter buyback activity in coming quarters compared to Q1. Management intends to remain active in buybacks but will prioritize preserving capital for a building loan pipeline.

Commercial Real Estate concentration and long-term targets

The long-term goal is to bring the CRE concentration ratio below 300% by rotating out of lower-ROI transactional clients. Management noted there is little external pressure to accelerate this runoff, as the existing loans remain high quality.

Asset quality trends in C&I and Office portfolios

The slight uptick in criticized loans was attributed to normal year-end financial collection cycles, with an overall downward trend expected for the year.
